# Quick start

Start with a project and a conversation. You’ll connect efference to a model, give it a
little context about your project, and choose what it can do without asking you. You can
work in the terminal first and add a browser or phone later.
<!-- src: src/bin/efference/setup.rs::default_verb; src/setup/handoff.rs::offer_project_setup; assets/guide/new-project.md; src/bin/efference/serve.rs::host -->

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://efference.net/install.sh | sh
```
<!-- TODO: the installer URL is generated by dist and does not exist yet. Confirm the exact command dist emits, what the installer writes besides the binary, and the release targets (macOS and Linux; no Windows). -->

efference runs on macOS and Linux. You’ll need `bash` for the agent’s commands. Git is
needed only if you want a session to work in its own **worktree**, a separate checkout of
your project.
<!-- src: src/tools/bash.rs; src/host/worktree.rs; src/bin/efference/island.rs (std::os::unix); src/platform/secrets.rs (macOS and Linux stores only) -->

To update later, run the install command again. To check for a newer version without
installing it, run `efference update --check`.
<!-- src: src/bin/efference/update.rs; src/platform/update_check.rs::INSTALL_COMMAND -->

## Open your project

```sh
cd ~/code/your-project
efference
```

On your first launch, setup walks you through connecting a model and preparing the
project. After that, `efference` opens a new-session form, or a short menu if this project
already has sessions: attach to one that is running, or resume an earlier one.
<!-- src: src/bin/efference/setup.rs::default_verb; src/bin/efference/picker.rs::run, menu; src/bin/efference/picker/app.rs::ask -->

### Connect a model

Choose how you want to reach a model: through Anthropic, OpenRouter, OpenAI, a ChatGPT
subscription, or another endpoint that speaks one of the same APIs. Give it a name, and
you have a **connection** — the provider and credentials efference will use for your
model requests.
<!-- src: src/setup.rs::PROVIDERS; src/setup/flow.rs::one_connection, describe_endpoint -->

For an API key, you can name an environment variable or paste the key into setup to keep
it in your OS keychain. A ChatGPT subscription uses browser sign-in instead. Setup records
where to find the credential in `~/.efference/config.toml`, not the key itself. You can
change or add connections later with `efference setup`.
<!-- src: src/setup/flow.rs::api_key_source; src/setup/flow/chatgpt.rs::chatgpt_source; src/setup/render.rs::HEADER; src/setup/flow.rs::run (existing connections -> manage::run) -->

If you choose an environment variable that isn’t set in this shell, setup tells you and
stops. Set it, then run `efference` again. [Credentials](credentials.md) covers the choices,
including starting efference through 1Password’s `op run`.
<!-- src: src/bin/efference/setup.rs::run -->

Setup also asks whether efference may check efference.net once a day for a newer version.
Say no and it won’t check on its own. [How efference runs](how-it-runs.md) explains what
the check sends; [Configuration](configuration.md) covers the rest of your settings.
<!-- src: src/setup/flow.rs::run; src/setup/updates.rs::ask_unless_answered -->

### Give the agent a starting point

If your project has no `efference.toml`, efference offers to help create one, in the
terminal or in your browser. You can also leave this for later. The file tells future
sessions what the project is for, what they should know, and what they may do without
asking you.
<!-- src: src/setup/handoff.rs::offer_project_setup; src/host/boot/scaffold.rs::CONFIG_SCAFFOLD; assets/guide/new-project.md -->

Project setup is itself an agent **session**: a conversation with a model, billed as
normal use. You choose the model on a form first. The agent then asks before reading your
files and talks through the project’s permissions and context with you. It writes
`efference.toml` and, if you don’t already have an agent guide, `AGENTS.md`. In a git
repository it also asks whose project this is, so it can keep efference’s own files out of
version control to match.
<!-- src: src/bin/efference/picker.rs::create_through_form; src/host/boot/scaffold.rs::CONFIG_SCAFFOLD; assets/guide/new-project.md -->

## Start a conversation

For a first task, try asking the agent to help you get oriented:

> Walk me through how this project is organized and how to run its tests. Don’t change
> anything yet.

From there, you can ask it to investigate a bug, make a change, or run checks. Your
project’s permissions decide which tool calls run without asking; calls held for review
wait for your decision. [Permissions](permissions.md) explains how to choose that balance.
<!-- src: src/agent/step.rs::run_call; src/agent/step/judge.rs::judge; src/config/policy.rs::classify -->

As it works, you’ll see tool results labelled with the lines the agent was shown.
[Triage](triage.md) explains how those excerpts are selected and how you can compare them
with the full output.
<!-- src: src/clients/tui/projection.rs::result_entry, selection_note; web/src/render/parse.ts::wireLabel; src/clients/tui/block_menu.rs::menu_items; web/src/ui/Inspector.tsx -->

## Keep working after you close the terminal

For your first session, you don’t need a background service. With no host already running,
`efference` runs in **standalone mode**: closing the terminal or quitting efference ends
the session. Its record stays in the project. Run `efference` there again and choose
“resume an archived session…” to pick it back up.
<!-- src: src/host/island.rs::OwnerWatch; src/host/island_exit.rs::archive_and_shut_down; src/bin/efference/picker.rs::resume_on; src/bin/efference/picker/app.rs::RESUME -->

When you want the agent to keep working while you’re away, start a **host**, the
long-lived process that holds your sessions, in a terminal you leave open:

```sh
efference --host
```

While that host runs, `efference` in any project uses it. Leaving the terminal interface
now **detaches** from the session instead of stopping it, so you can come back later.
[How efference runs](how-it-runs.md) explains the two modes and running a host as a
service. For a browser on your computer or phone, continue to
[Remote access](remote-access.md).
<!-- src: src/bin/efference/cli.rs::host_candidates; src/clients/tui/control_strip.rs::strip_live_items -->
